title: Buy what you know
topic: A tax-free account and a familiar feeling

messages.text: Opened my new NISA. Only Japanese companies
I know them. I use their products every day
Foreign shares are a gamble anyway
I have ¥12 million on deposit doing nothing. Maybe it's time

steps.title: 58 · school administrator in Tokyo
steps.body: Michiko retires at 65. She has saved **¥12,000,000** (about €72,700), almost all of it in a bank deposit, like many Japanese households. Her colleagues are starting to invest. Their first instinct: stay at home.

steps.title: 新NISA · new NISA
steps.body: Since 2024, a bigger version of Japan's [[tax-free-account]]: gains inside it are not taxed. The state promotes it with the slogan "from savings to investment". The account decides the tax. What goes inside decides the risk.

steps.prompt: Swipe each sentence: a feeling or a fact?

items.text: I use their products every day, so they're safe
Japan is about 5% of the world's stock market
Gains inside a NISA are not taxed
A broad world fund holds thousands of companies in many countries

steps.explanation: Knowing a company's products doesn't make its shares less risky. Familiar feels safe: that pull is called [[home-bias]].

steps.prompt: Michiko moves money into a NISA. What changes?
options: Gains inside are not taxed; the risk depends on what she buys
Her money becomes guaranteed by the state
Her money can no longer fall
steps.explanation: A tax-free account is a wrapper. It changes the tax on gains, not how much the investments inside can rise or fall.

t1.body: Michiko will stop working at 65. She saved **¥12,000,000** (about €72,700). Almost all of it is in the bank, like for many people in Japan. Her friends at work start to invest. They want to buy only Japanese companies.

t2.body: Since 2024 Japan has a bigger version of this account. You pay no tax on gains inside it. This is a [[tax-free-account]]. The account changes the tax. What you put inside it decides the risk.

so1.prompt: Swipe each sentence: is it a feeling or a fact?
so1.explanation: Knowing a company's products doesn't make its shares safer. We like what we know. This is called [[home-bias]].

q1.prompt: Michiko puts money in a NISA. What changes?
options: She pays no tax on gains. The risk depends on what she buys
Her money can't go down any more
q1.explanation: The account only changes the tax. The things inside can still go up and down.
